originalTitle: Analysis: How Trump could reignite the Fed independence fight after Warsh's rate hike
summary: The Federal Reserve unanimously raised interest rates by a quarter point despite repeated calls from President Donald Trump for lower rates.
content:
Chairman Kevin Warsh's quarter-point rate increase sends an unambiguous message to President Donald Trump: Hands off the Federal Reserve .

Warsh on Wednesday voted with a unanimous Federal Open Market Committee to raise interest rates by a quarter-point, despite repeated urgings by Trump and his administration to cut or at least not hike. Those warnings continued even as the FOMC convened Wednesday. Yet Warsh reviewed the economy and made up his own mind that interest rates needed to rise, despite the potential political consequences.

Warsh made no reference to politics in his press conference but said he was worried about inflation that remained stuck above the Fed's 2% target.

Warsh chuckled when asked by a reporter if he had a message for Trump and politely declined to answer. "I've got nothing for you on a discussion with the president."

Read more CNBC politics and policy coverage

White House spokesman Kush Desai said on Fox News after Warsh's press conference that he hadn't spoken to Trump, but said the president's desire for cuts was clear.

"Certainly today's rather unfortunate decision by the Federal Reserve to hike interest rates was not, from the administration's point of view, backed by a particularly compelling economic case," Desai said.

Trump later seemed to address the Fed's decision in a Truth Social post that didn't mention Warsh by name. "Interest Rates in the United States should be 1%, or less, because we are the Best Credit in the World — BY FAR," Trump wrote.

Trump selected Warsh to run the Fed in January after souring on former Chair Jerome Powell, whom Trump appointed in his first term. Trump was furious at Powell for, among other things, voting to cut interest rates by a half-point in September 2024. Trump thought that decision was an attempt throw the election to the incumbent Democratic administration in the November presidential election. Powell then, like Warsh now, said he looked only at the economy in making his decisions.

Trump has said he trusts Warsh to make good decisions. People close to the president have said Warsh could make the same decisions as Powell and get a different response. Before Wednesday's rate decision, Trump wrote off Warsh's decisions to hold interest rates steady — rather than cut — at FOMC meetings in June and July as the result of other Fed voters making political decisions.

That position will be difficult to maintain now that Warsh has voted with the FOMC to raise interest rates.

Trump administration members have argued the Fed ought not to intervene on the economy now, saying there is a tradition of the Fed not intervening ahead of midterm elections. That idea isn't well-supported by the historical record.

Since 1994, when the Fed began making same-day announcements of changes in its interest rate policies, the Fed has changed interest rates with as much or less time on the calendar in advance of an election as there is now in five election years: 1998, 2004, 2008, 2018, and 2022.

Some Democrats have bitterly complained since Warsh's nomination that he won't be independent of the president who chose him. Wednesday's rate decision suggests they may have been too early to judge him.

Trump and Warsh have a longstanding relationship, and the two men have spoken directly since Warsh took office, the president has said. Warsh also meets often with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, and the two men are friends.

If Trump doesn't like what Warsh is doing, there is much he can do beyond merely telling Warsh through one of those channels.

Trump in 2025 attempted to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook . The Supreme Court blocked that action , saying Trump hadn't followed the appropriate process. "At minimum, Cook was entitled to some explanation of the evidence at issue, some avenue for a response, and a deadline by which a response would be due," the Supreme Court wrote.

Last month, Trump restarted the process of firing Cook. The administration sent the Fed governor a letter saying Trump was considering firing her and demanded a response by Aug. 26. She sent that response , and now the ball is in the administration's court.

Trump could fire Cook again at any time. That decision would likely need to be reviewed by the courts.

Trump's Department of Justice also opened and then closed an investigation into Powell pending a separate inquiry by the Fed's inspector general into cost overruns in building renovations. The DOJ has said it reserves the right to reopen that investigation once the IG issues its report, which could come at any time.

A consultant is looking on behalf of the Fed into the 2023 failure of Silicon Valley Bank, an institution overseen by the Fed. Some analysts believe the investigation could give the administration a pretext to fire Michael Barr , the Fed official who was in charge of bank supervision in 2023. Barr stepped down from that regulatory job but still has a seat on the Fed's board.

If Trump takes any of those actions, it will end the administration's tacit truce on the Fed that has held since he picked Warsh.

But if there's anyone who's surprised by Warsh, it shouldn't be the president. He liked all the candidates he was considering for the Fed, he said back in January, before picking Warsh.

"Problem is they change once they get the job," Trump said . "Sort of disloyalty, but they got to do what they think is right."
chineseTitle: 分析：沃什加息后特朗普如何重燃美联储独立斗争
chineseSummary: 尽管唐纳德·特朗普总统一再呼吁降低利率，但美联储还是一致将利率提高了四分之一个百分点。
chineseContent:
主席凯文·沃什 (Kevin Warsh) 加息四分之一个百分点向唐纳德·特朗普总统发出了明确的信息：放开美联储。

尽管特朗普及其政府一再敦促降息或至少不加息，沃什周三与联邦公开市场委员会一致投票决定将利率提高四分之一个百分点。即使联邦公开市场委员会周三召开会议，这些警告仍在继续。然而，沃什回顾了经济情况，并下定决心，尽管可能产生潜在的政治后果，但利率需要上升。

沃什在新闻发布会上没有提及政治，但表示他担心通胀仍高于美联储 2% 的目标。

当记者问沃什是否有话要给特朗普时，沃什笑了，并礼貌地拒绝回答。 “关于与总统的讨论，我没有什么可以告诉你的。”

阅读更多 CNBC 政治和政策报道

白宫发言人库什·德赛在沃什新闻发布会后对福克斯新闻表示，他没有与特朗普交谈过，但表示总统对削减开支的愿望是明确的。

德赛表示：“当然，从政府的角度来看，美联储今天相当不幸的加息决定并没有得到特别令人信服的经济案例的支持。”

特朗普后来似乎在《真相社会》的一篇帖子中谈到了美联储的决定，但没有提到沃什的名字。特朗普写道：“美国的利率应该为 1% 或更低，因为我们是迄今为止世界上最好的信用国。”

特朗普在对特朗普在第一个任期内任命的前主席杰罗姆·鲍威尔(Jerome Powell)感到不满后，于一月份选择沃什担任美联储主席。特朗普对鲍威尔在 2024 年 9 月投票降息半个百分点等行为感到愤怒。特朗普认为这一决定是试图在 11 月总统选举中将选举权推给现任民主党政府。当时的鲍威尔和现在的沃什一样，表示他在做出决定时只考虑经济情况。

特朗普表示，他相信沃什能够做出正确的决定。接近总统的人士表示，沃什可能会做出与鲍威尔相同的决定，但会得到不同的回应。在周三的利率决定之前，特朗普取消了沃什在 6 月和 7 月 FOMC 会议上保持利率稳定（而不是降息）的决定，因为其他美联储选民做出了政治决定。

既然沃什已经投票支持联邦公开市场委员会(FOMC)加息，那么这一立场将很难维持。

特朗普政府成员认为，美联储现在不应该干预经济，称美联储在中期选举之前有不干预经济的传统。这个想法并没有得到历史记录的充分支持。

自1994年美联储开始在同一天宣布其利率政策变化以来，美联储在选举前调整利率的时间与现在五个选举年（1998年、2004年、2008年、2018年和2022年）的时间一样长或更少。

自沃什获得提名以来，一些民主党人强烈抱怨他不会独立于选择他的总统。周三的利率决定表明，他们对他做出判断可能还为时过早。

总统表示，特朗普和沃什有着长期的关系，自沃什上任以来，两人一直直接交谈。沃什还经常与财政部长斯科特·贝森特会面，两人是朋友。

如果特朗普不喜欢沃什的所作所为，他可以做很多事情，而不仅仅是通过这些渠道之一告诉沃什。

特朗普于 2025 年试图解雇美联储理事丽莎·库克。最高法院阻止了这一行动，称特朗普没有遵循适当的程序。最高法院写道：“至少，库克有权获得对相关证据的一些解释、某种回应途径以及回应的最后期限。”

上个月，特朗普重启了解雇库克的程序。政府致信美联储理事，称特朗普正在考虑解雇她，并要求在 8 月 26 日之前做出回应。她发出了回应，现在决定权在政府手中。

特朗普随时可以再次解雇库克。该决定可能需要由法院审查。

特朗普的司法部也对鲍威尔展开了调查，然后结束了调查，等待美联储监察长对建筑翻修成本超支进行单独调查。司法部表示，一旦监察长随时发布报告，它保留重新启动调查的权利。

一名顾问正在代表美联储调查美联储监管机构硅谷银行 2023 年的倒闭。一些分析师认为，这项调查可能为政府提供解雇2023年负责银行监管的美联储官员迈克尔·巴尔(Michael Barr)的借口。巴尔辞去了监管职务，但仍拥有美联储董事会席位。

如果特朗普采取任何这些行动，这将结束自他选择沃什以来政府与美联储之间的默契休战。

但如果有人对沃什感到惊讶，那应该不是总统。一月份他在选择沃什之前曾表示，他喜欢他正在考虑的所有美联储候选人。

“问题是他们一旦得到这份工作就会改变，”特朗普说。 “有点不忠诚，但他们必须做他们认为正确的事情。”
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
